options.text: Stay inside until you know it's safe.

options.text: Run to the front yard to meet them.

options.text: Tell them to put the fire out before helping your husband.

options.text: You can hang up now, I'm done.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller

transcript_en.text: Hello! My brother left a burning mosquito coil on top of a plastic stool and now the stool is melting and catching fire!

options.text: Sit in the living room and wait.

options.text: Just go back inside and check if the fire died down.

options.text: Evacuate the house immediately. Go outside to a safe area.

options.text: Stay inside and open the front windows.

options.text: Try to use the store microphone yourself to call your parents.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: I am standing with the security guard now. He is talking to me. He says he will keep me safe.

options.text: Excellent. Stay with the guard. Ask him to call for your parents over the store loudspeaker. Keep on the line with me.
options.label: safe

options.text: You can hang up now since the guard is there.

options.text: Ask the guard to take you to a restaurant for lunch.
options.label: unsafe

options.text: Tell the guard to leave his post to search the aisles.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: The guard made the announcement. We are waiting at the front desk. I hope my parents hear it.

options.text: I am sending BFP to search the building. Wait outside on the curb.

options.text: I am sending MDRRMO medical. Go sit in the delivery loading dock.
options.label: unsafe

options.text: Do not dispatch anyone. Supermarket staff always handle this.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Failing to dispatch assistance for a lost child violates standard safety protocols.

options.text: Go outside and tell the men they cannot dump trash there.

options.text: What does the trash smell like?

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: We are at Barangay Labuin. The men are still dumping and it looks like some liquid is leaking from the plastic drums!

options.text: Stay inside. Can you safely see the plate number of the blue truck from your window?

options.text: Go outside to take a close-up photo of the liquid leak.

options.text: Open your window and yell at them.

options.text: Run to the truck and try to pull the bags back onto their vehicle.
options.label: unsafe

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: The plate number is TTT-987. They are finishing up and getting back inside the truck cab.

options.text: Run outside and block the road so they cannot drive away.

options.text: Follow the truck on your bicycle.

options.text: Call your neighbors to start a protest.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: The truck turned right toward the main bypass road. The empty lot is left dirty with bags and leaking drums.

options.text: Stay inside. I am dispatching PNP to investigate the illegal dumping and trace the vehicle. Do not touch the dumped items.

options.text: I am sending BFP. Go outside to clean up the spilled trash.

options.text: I am sending MDRRMO medical. Go check if the liquid is hot.

options.text: Do not dispatch anyone. The rain will wash the spill away.

options.text: Go try to take the spray cans away from them.

options.text: What words are they spray-painting?
options.label: unsafe

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: We are near the slide at the barangay plaza. One of them has a big wooden stick and is hitting the swings!

options.text: Keep watching from safety. Can you describe what the kid with the stick is wearing?
options.label: safe

options.text: Go try to grab the stick when he puts it down.
options.label: unsafe

options.text: Throw pebbles at them to make them stop.
options.label: unsafe

options.text: Run and hide in the bushes right next to the swings.
options.label: unsafe

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: He is wearing a black hoodie and a yellow cap. The others are laughing and taking videos on their phones.

options.text: Thank you. Stay where you are, behind a safe structure. Do not let them see you watching.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Maintaining caller safety and anonymity is paramount during active crime reporting.

options.text: Take out your phone and walk closer to take a selfie with them.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Approaching vandals to take photos is highly dangerous and provocative.

options.text: Call your friends to come start a fight with them.
options.label: unsafe

options.text: Confront them and say you are recording them.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: I am standing behind the plaza concrete bench. They are still breaking the wood. Please send help.

options.text: Stay behind the bench. I am dispatching PNP to handle the vandalism. Do not get closer.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Dispatching PNP to handle property destruction and keeping the caller safe is the correct resolution.

options.text: I am sending BFP. Go help them break the rest of the bench.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: BFP is incorrect, and encouraging vandalism is illegal and unsafe.

options.text: I am sending MDRRMO medical. Go stand next to the kid with the stick.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Standing next to armed vandals is highly dangerous, and medical units are incorrect.

options.text: Do not dispatch anyone. The park will clean it up tomorrow.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Failing to dispatch law enforcement to active property destruction is negligent.

transcript_en.text: Hello! I am at the plaza and there is a large, heavy-looking backpack left on a bench near the bandstand. It has been sitting here for over an hour and nobody is around!

options.text: 911, what is your exact location at the plaza? Move away from the backpack and do not touch it.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Getting the location is key, and instructing the caller not to touch unattended baggage prevents injury from potential hazardous contents.

options.text: Open the backpack to search for a name tag inside.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Opening unattended, suspicious luggage can trigger explosives or expose the caller to hazardous chemicals.

options.text: What color is the zipper on the backpack?
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Asking minor details wastes critical seconds during a potential package threat.

options.text: Kick the backpack to see if it makes a noise.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Kicking or shaking suspicious packages is extremely hazardous.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: We are near the bandstand at Sta. Cruz Plaza. I moved to the walkway about 10 meters away.

options.text: Keep that safe distance. Tell other park-goers nearby to also stay away from the bench. Do not lose sight of the bag.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Keeping civilians clear prevents injuries while the dispatcher coordinates police verification.

options.text: Go stand right next to the bag to guard it from thieves.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Standing next to a suspicious unattended package puts the caller in the direct blast/hazard zone.

options.text: Try to drag the bag to the trash bin to keep the park clean.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Moving the package is highly dangerous and shouldn't be done.

options.text: Shine a laser pointer at the bag to test it.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Shining lasers is useless and can distract others or trigger photoelectric sensors in rare cases.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: I told a family walking by, and they moved away. The bag is still sitting on the bench alone.

options.text: Excellent. Stay at your safe distance. I am forwarding this information to our field officers.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Reassuring the caller and maintaining a safe boundary is the standard response for suspicious packages.

options.text: Pour water on the bag to soak it.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Soaking suspicious items can damage electrical triggers or cause chemical reactions.

options.text: Try to throw stones at the bag from far away.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Throwing stones can impact and set off any unstable materials inside.

options.text: Ask a random kid to go pick it up.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Putting other children in danger is highly irresponsible and dangerous.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: We are still standing on the walkway. Nobody has approached the bench. Please send help.

options.text: Stay there. I am dispatching PNP to inspect the unattended backpack. Do not get closer.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Dispatching PNP to secure and inspect unattended items in public spaces is correct.

options.text: I am sending BFP. Go pick up the bag to hand it to them.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: BFP is incorrect, and picking up suspicious packages violates all safety protocols.

options.text: I am sending MDRRMO medical. Go sit on the bench next to the bag to wait.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Sitting next to the bag is highly dangerous, and medical transport is incorrect.

options.text: Do not dispatch anyone. Someone just forgot their school bag.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Ignoring suspicious unattended items in public gathering zones is highly negligent.

transcript_en.text: 911, what is your emergency?

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: Hello! There is a small black drone with flashing lights flying very low over our backyard. It keeps hovering right outside my bedroom window and recording!

options.text: 911, what is your exact address? Go inside your house and close the window curtains.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Acquiring the address is the first step, and closing curtains immediately stops the invasion of privacy.

options.text: Stand outside and throw rocks at the drone to crash it.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Throwing rocks at an active drone can damage it, cause it to fall on you, or anger the operator.

options.text: What brand of drone is it?
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Asking about drone brands wastes critical time during an active privacy violation.

options.text: Try to spray the drone with a garden hose.
options.label: unsafe

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: We are at Barangay Duhat. I am in my bedroom with the curtains closed now. The drone is still buzzing outside.

options.text: Stay inside. Can you safely peek and see if there is anyone standing on the street nearby holding a remote controller?
options.label: safe

options.text: Climb onto the roof to get closer to the drone.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Climbing roofs exposes the child caller to falling hazards and direct contact with drone blades.

options.text: Open your window and yell at the drone.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Yelling at a machine is useless and exposes your face to the drone's camera again.

options.text: Try to catch the drone with a butterfly net from the window.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Leaning out of windows to catch spinning drone propellers causes severe hand lacerations.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: I see a man standing next to a motorcycle down the street holding a controller. He keeps looking up toward my window.

options.text: Good. Stay inside and keep your curtains closed. Note down the color of his shirt and the motorcycle.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Gathering descriptions helps police identify the suspect operator upon arrival.

options.text: Go outside to confront the man yourself.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Confronting suspicious strangers holding equipment is highly dangerous for children.

options.text: Call your parents to go confront the man.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Prompting confrontations can lead to verbal or physical fights; let police handle it.

options.text: Flash a mirror at the man to blind his view.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Flashing mirrors is provocative and doesn't solve the privacy violation.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: He is wearing a grey jacket and has a red motorcycle. The drone is still hovering near our roof.

options.text: Stay inside. I am dispatching PNP to check the operator and the low-flying drone. Keep safe.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Dispatching PNP to handle privacy violations and suspicious drone operation is correct.

options.text: I am sending BFP. Go outside to wave them down.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: BFP is incorrect for drone privacy issues, and going outside exposes the child.

options.text: I am sending MDRRMO medical. Go tell the man to leave.

options.text: Do not dispatch anyone. Drones are just toys.
options.label: unsafe

transcript_en.text: 911, what is your emergency?

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: Hello! My brother fell off his bicycle onto the asphalt road. He has a large, dirty scrape on his knee that is bleeding a lot and he is crying in pain!

options.text: 911, what is your exact address? Help your brother sit down in a safe spot.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Acquiring the location is the first requirement, and sitting down prevents further injury or falling.

options.text: Tell your brother to walk it off and ride his bike home.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Forcing someone with a bleeding injury to walk or ride a bike can worsen the wound and cause more pain.

options.text: What color is the bicycle?
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Asking about the bicycle color is irrelevant and wastes time during a medical event.

options.text: Rub the scrape with a dry towel to clean the dirt.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Rubbing a fresh scrape with a dry towel will cause intense pain, damage the tissue further, and push dirt deeper.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: We are at Barangay Callios, near the basketball court. He is sitting on the sidewalk. There is dirt and gravel stuck in the scrape.

options.text: If you have clean water, gently pour it over the scrape to wash away the dirt. Do not scrub it.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Gently rinsing with clean water washes away surface dirt and bacteria without damaging the raw skin.

options.text: Use a sewing needle to scrape the gravel out of the wound.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Using unsterile needles to dig in a wound causes extreme pain and risks deep infection.

options.text: Pour rubbing alcohol directly on the raw scrape.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Pouring alcohol directly on large raw scrapes causes extreme, unnecessary pain and delays tissue healing.

options.text: Blow on the wound to dry the blood.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Blowing on a wound introduces mouth bacteria, increasing the risk of infection.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: I poured water from my water bottle over his knee. The dirt is gone and it's mostly clean, but it's still bleeding.

options.text: Press a clean cloth or tissue gently but firmly directly on the scrape to stop the bleeding.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Applying direct, gentle pressure with a clean fabric helps the blood clot and stops the bleeding.

options.text: Squeeze the leg tightly above the knee to stop the blood.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Trying to restrict blood flow (like a tourniquet) is dangerous and unnecessary for a simple road scrape.

options.text: Have him stand up and bend his knee repeatedly.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Bending the joint pulls the raw skin apart and will cause the bleeding to start again.

options.text: Put mud on the scrape to scab it over.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Putting mud on open wounds introduces dangerous bacteria, including tetanus.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: I am holding a clean tissue on it. The bleeding has slowed down. He has stopped crying but his knee is very sore.

options.text: Keep holding the pressure. I am dispatching MDRRMO to check the injury and clean it properly. Do not let him walk.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Dispatching MDRRMO for medical assessment and maintaining pressure is the correct resolution.

options.text: I am sending a fire truck. Go back to riding the bicycle.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: BFP is incorrect for basic medical scrapes, and riding is unsafe for the injured knee.

options.text: I am sending PNP. Go walk down the road to meet them.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Walking on an injured knee is unsafe, and police are incorrect for direct medical assessment.

options.text: Do not dispatch anyone. Just let the wound dry in the sun.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Failing to dispatch assistance or advise proper covering leaves the wound open to infection.

transcript_en.text: 911, what is your emergency?

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: Hello! My sister was frying fish and hot oil splattered onto her forearm. It is very red and she is crying because it hurts so much!

options.text: 911, what is your exact address? Keep your sister away from the hot stove.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Determining the address is the first priority, and moving away from the hot stove prevents further accidents.

options.text: Put a large piece of ice directly on the burn.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Putting ice directly on a burn can damage the delicate skin tissues further and cause frostbite-like damage.

options.text: What kind of fish was she frying?
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Asking about food types is irrelevant and wastes time during a medical emergency.

options.text: Pop any blisters that are starting to form.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Popping blisters breaks the skin barrier, exposing the raw wound to infection.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: We are at Barangay Patimbao. She is sitting at the dining table. The burn skin is very red and starting to swell.

options.text: Gently run cool tap water over the burn for 10 to 15 minutes. Do not scrub it.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Cool running water safely cools the burn, stops the burning process, and numbs the pain.

options.text: Spread toothpaste all over the burn.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Toothpaste traps heat in the burn, can introduce chemical irritation, and makes it harder for doctors to clean.

options.text: Rub butter or cooking oil on the burn.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Butter and oils trap heat, worsening the burn damage and introducing infection risks.

options.text: Scrub the burn with soap and a rough sponge.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Scrubbing burned skin causes intense pain and rips away protective skin layers.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: She is holding her arm under the kitchen tap. She says the cool water makes it feel much better.

options.text: Good. Keep it under the water. If you have a clean, dry cloth, you can cover it loosely after cooling. Do not wrap it tightly.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Covering loosely protects the sensitive skin from dirt and air irritation without pressing on it.

options.text: Wrap it tightly with a plastic bag to keep the air out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Wrapping tightly traps moisture and heat, and plastic can stick to raw skin, causing pain when removed.

options.text: Put a tight adhesive bandage directly over the whole burn.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Adhesive bandages will stick to the burned skin and pull it off during removal.

options.text: Spray perfume on the arm to sanitize it.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Perfume contains alcohol and chemicals that cause extreme burning pain on damaged skin.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: We cooled it for 10 minutes and I covered it loosely with a clean cotton towel. She is much calmer now.

options.text: Great job. I am dispatching MDRRMO to evaluate the burn and dress it. Stay on the line.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Dispatching MDRRMO for professional burn assessment is the correct final step.

options.text: I will send a fire truck. Go back to cooking dinner.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Fire trucks do not provide direct ambulance transport, and cooking is unsafe right now.

options.text: I will send a police patrol. Tell your sister to walk to the plaza.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Police cars are not medical transport, and walking is unnecessary.

options.text: Do not dispatch anyone. Minor burns heal in an hour.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Failing to dispatch assistance leaves potentially severe oil burns untreated.

transcript_en.text: 911, what is your emergency?

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: Hello! My brother was playing tag outside in the hot sun and his nose suddenly started bleeding very heavily! The blood is dropping all over his shirt!

options.text: 911, what is your exact location? Have your brother sit down and lean slightly forward.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Getting the address is the first step, and leaning forward prevents blood from running down the throat.

options.text: Tell him to tilt his head far back to stop the flow.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Tilting the head back causes blood to run down the throat, which can cause choking or vomiting.

options.text: Have him lie flat on his back on the grass.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Lying flat makes blood flow down the airway, which is a choking hazard.

options.text: What game were you playing?
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Asking about game details wastes critical time during a medical call.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: We are at Barangay Labuin, next to the chapel. He is sitting on the steps leaning forward, but the blood is still dripping.

options.text: Use a clean tissue or cloth and pinch the soft part of his nose shut. Tell him to breathe through his mouth.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Pinching the soft part of the nose applies direct pressure to the bleeding vessels, stopping the nosebleed.

options.text: Stuff dry rolled-up paper towels deep inside both nostrils.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Shoving paper deep in the nose can scratch the lining and cause worse bleeding when removed.

options.text: Tell him to blow his nose as hard as he can to clear the blood.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Blowing the nose disrupts early clots and causes the bleeding to worsen.

options.text: Pour cold water directly down his throat.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Pouring water down the throat of someone with active nasal bleeding is a severe choking hazard.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: I am pinching the soft part of his nose and he is breathing through his mouth. We have been holding it for a few minutes.

options.text: Keep holding the pinch continuously for at least 10 minutes. If you have a cold damp cloth, you can place it on his forehead or bridge of the nose.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Holding for a full 10 minutes ensures the clot forms, and a cold compress helps constrict blood vessels.

options.text: Pinch the nose for 5 seconds, release to check, and pinch again.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Releasing the pressure too early disrupts the clotting process and keeps it bleeding.

options.text: Slap him gently on the back of the neck.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Slapping the neck is useless and does nothing to stop nasal bleeding.

options.text: Tell him to swallow the blood that is in his mouth.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Swallowing blood irritates the stomach lining and will cause nausea and vomiting.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: We held it for 10 minutes and released. The bleeding has stopped completely! He is feeling better but a bit dizzy.

options.text: Keep him sitting quietly in the shade. I am dispatching MDRRMO to check on him. Do not let him run around.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Dispatching MDRRMO to verify the child's status after heavy bleeding and heat exposure is the correct resolution.

options.text: I will send BFP. Go back to playing tag in the sun.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: BFP is incorrect for medical events, and running in the sun risks re-triggering the bleed.

options.text: I will send a PNP patrol. Tell him to walk to the main road.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Making a dizzy child walk on the road is hazardous, and police are incorrect.

options.text: Do not dispatch anyone. He is fine now.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Failing to dispatch assistance leaves a dizzy child vulnerable to heat stroke.

options.text: How high was the garden wall?
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Asking about height details is minor, but locating and securing the patient is the priority.

options.text: Pull the foot hard to 'pop' the ankle back in place.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: We are at Barangay Patimbao. He is sitting on a chair now, but his ankle looks twice its normal size.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: Hello! My brother was riding his bike on the side of the road when a speeding motorcycle hit him and drove off without stopping! My brother is lying on the grass, his leg is bleeding, and he can't get up!

options.text: 911, what is your exact location? Stay with your brother on the grass, out of the road.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Securing the location is key, and keeping off the road prevents being hit by other passing vehicles.

options.text: Chase the motorcycle on your own bike to get the plate number.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Chasing a hit-and-run suspect on a bicycle is extremely dangerous and leaves the injured brother alone.

options.text: What brand of motorcycle was it?
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Asking about motorcycle brands is minor, but locating and securing the patient is the priority.

options.text: Drag your brother to the middle of the road so cars can see him.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Dragging an injured person into the road exposes them to oncoming traffic and severe danger.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: We are on the shoulder of the road near the big mango tree in Barangay Callios. The motorcycle was red and drove toward the town plaza.

options.text: Okay. Tell your brother to stay completely still. If you have a clean cloth, apply gentle pressure to his bleeding leg. Do not move him.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Keeping the patient still prevents worsening potential fractures, and gentle pressure helps control bleeding.

options.text: Try to help him stand up and walk to the mango tree.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Moving someone with a potential leg fracture can cause severe pain and deeper bone/nerve damage.

options.text: Pour hot coffee from your thermos on his bleeding leg.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Hot liquids cause severe burns and do not treat bleeding or sanitize wounds.

options.text: Run down the road to ask cars for help.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Running into traffic to flag cars is extremely dangerous for a child.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: I am holding my clean handkerchief on his scrape. The bleeding is slowing down. He is lying still.

options.text: Good. Stay where you are. Did you notice any other details about the motorcycle driver, like his shirt color?
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Gathering suspect descriptions helps police intercept the fleeing hit-and-run driver.

options.text: Leave your brother to search the grass for pieces of the motorcycle.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Wandering around looking for debris wastes time and leaves the patient unattended.

options.text: Shout at passing cars that they are bad drivers.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Provoking drivers is unsafe and does not help the emergency.

options.text: Tell your brother it was his fault for riding there.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Blaming the victim causes distress and is unprofessional.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: The driver had a black helmet and a yellow jacket. We are waiting on the grassy shoulder.

options.text: Thank you. I am dispatching MDRRMO to treat and transport your brother, and PNP to investigate the hit-and-run. Stay in place.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Dispatching MDRRMO for medical care and PNP to investigate the traffic crime is the correct joint response.

options.text: I will send BFP. Go wait in the middle of the road.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: BFP is incorrect for traffic accidents, and standing in the road is highly dangerous.

options.text: I am sending PNP only. Tell your brother to carry his bike home.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The brother is injured and cannot carry a bike; medical transport (MDRRMO) is essential.

options.text: Do not dispatch anyone. Hit-and-run drivers are never caught.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Ignoring a hit-and-run report with an injured child is highly negligent.

transcript_en.text: 911, what is your emergency?

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: Hello! A grass fire in the empty field next to our street has spread to the wooden power pole! The pole is catching fire and the overhead wires are starting to spark and sag!

options.text: 911, what is your exact address? Stay far away from the power pole and sagging wires.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Confirming the address is critical, and staying clear of sagging wires prevents fatal electrical shock.

options.text: Try to pull the sagging wires away with a wooden stick.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Touching live high-voltage power lines with anything, even wood, can cause fatal electrocution.

options.text: What color was the grass in the field?
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Asking about grass color wastes time during an active electrical and fire threat.

options.text: Throw a bucket of water at the burning pole.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Throwing water on a live electrical pole can conduct electricity back to the caller, causing electrocution.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: We are at Barangay Santa Angel Central. The wind is blowing sparks from the pole toward our front gate!

options.text: Move away from the gate. Evacuate to the back of your property or go to a neighbor's house away from the wires.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Moving away from falling sparks and sagging wires ensures safety from electrical and fire hazards.

options.text: Stand under the wires to watch them spark.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Standing under sagging, sparking wires puts the caller in danger of being hit if they snap.

options.text: Try to climb the gate to see the field better.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Climbing metal gates near sparking power lines risks electric shock if the gate becomes energized.

options.text: Open the gate to let the smoke escape.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Opening the gate wastes time and brings the caller closer to the sagging wires.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: We are in the neighbor's garden now. One of the wires just snapped and fell right across our street, blocking all traffic!

options.text: Do not go near the fallen wire. Stay in the neighbor's garden and warn anyone who tries to drive down the street.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Fallen wires can still be live and highly dangerous; warning others prevents accidents.

options.text: Run out to coil the snapped wire neatly.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Touching a snapped power line is extremely dangerous and almost certainly fatal.

options.text: Throw a dry branch on the wire to see if it sparks.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Playing with live high-voltage wires is highly dangerous and can trigger explosions.

options.text: Pour water on the street road to cool the wire.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Water on the street will conduct the electrical current, electrifying the puddle and road area.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: We are staying back. A car stopped at the end of the street because we waved at them. The pole is still burning.

options.text: Excellent job. I am dispatching BFP to extinguish the pole fire, and PNP to block the street and secure the live wire area.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Dispatching BFP for the fire and PNP to manage traffic and secure the live wire hazard is correct.

options.text: I am sending MDRRMO only. Go check if the power is still on in your house.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Medical units cannot resolve fires or live wires, and entering the house near sagging wires is unsafe.

options.text: I am sending PNP only. Go touch the wire with a dry leaf to check it.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Instructing anyone to touch a fallen wire is extremely dangerous and forbidden.

options.text: Do not dispatch anyone. Power poles burn out quickly.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Failing to dispatch BFP and PNP will allow the fire to spread and risks public electrocution.

transcript_en.text: 911, what is your emergency?

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: Hello! I am at the small grocery store and a man just snatched cash from the register and ran out the door! The elderly lady clerk got so scared that she fainted and hit her head on the counter!

options.text: 911, what is the name and address of the store? Stay with the clerk and do not chase the thief.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Acquiring the location is the priority, and staying back prevents the child from confronting a thief.

options.text: Chase the thief down the street to get the cash back.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Chasing a criminal can lead to a violent confrontation and leaves the unconscious clerk unattended.

options.text: What color was the cash register?
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Asking about cash register colors is irrelevant and wastes time during a medical event.

options.text: Shake the clerk vigorously by her shoulders to wake her up.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Shaking someone who fainted and hit their head can worsen neck or head injuries.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: We are at Barangay Callios, next to the pharmacy. The clerk is lying on the floor behind the counter. She is breathing but not waking up.

options.text: Keep her lying flat on her back. If she has no neck pain, gently elevate her feet about 12 inches using a box or cushion.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Lying flat and elevating the feet improves blood flow to the brain, helping a fainted person recover safely.

options.text: Pour cold water directly onto her face to splash her awake.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Splashing water on an unconscious person can cause them to choke or inhale water into their lungs.

options.text: Try to drag her outside to the sidewalk.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Moving an injured person unnecessarily can worsen spinal or head trauma.

options.text: Give her some medicine from the store shelves.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Administering drugs to an unconscious person is highly dangerous and a choking hazard.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: I put a box of tissue under her feet. She just opened her eyes and says her head hurts where she bumped it.

options.text: Tell her to remain lying down. Do not let her stand up yet. Can you describe what the thief was wearing?
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Keeping her down prevents another fall due to dizziness, and gathering descriptions helps PNP track the suspect.

options.text: Help her stand up immediately to check the cash registers.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Standing up too quickly after fainting can cause sudden dizziness and a second fall.

options.text: Run out to look for the thief's footprints.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Leaving the victim alone to search for clues is unsafe and unhelpful.

options.text: Slap her cheeks to keep her awake.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Slapping is aggressive, unnecessary, and can cause injury.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: The thief had a green shirt and a black backpack. The clerk is sitting up slowly but feels dizzy.

options.text: Tell her to sit still. I am dispatching PNP to investigate the theft, and MDRRMO to check her head injury. Stay there.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Dispatching PNP for the theft crime and MDRRMO for head trauma/fainting evaluation is the correct joint response.

options.text: I am sending BFP only. Go wait outside the store door.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: BFP is incorrect for theft and medical issues, and leaving the victim is unsafe.

options.text: I am sending PNP only. Tell the clerk to go home.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The clerk is dizzy and needs medical assessment (MDRRMO); sending PNP only is insufficient.

options.text: Do not dispatch anyone. The money was probably insured.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Failing to assist during theft and injury is negligent.

transcript_en.text: 911, what is your emergency?

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: Help! A fallen tree branch snapped the low utility line on our street. The wire is sparking on our bamboo fence, catching the fence on fire, and the live wire is blocking our driveway!

options.text: 911, what is your exact address? Keep away from the fence and the wire on the ground.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Acquiring the address is the first priority, and staying clear of live wires prevents fatal electrocution.

options.text: Try to move the wire out of the driveway with a metal rake.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Metal conducts electricity; touching a live wire with a metal tool will cause a fatal shock.

options.text: What kind of tree did the branch fall from?
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Asking about tree types wastes critical time during an active fire and electrical hazard.

options.text: Throw a bucket of water on the burning fence near the wire.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Water conducts electricity; throwing it near a live wire risks electrocution.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: We are at Barangay Patimbao. The fence is catching fire quickly and the smoke is starting to get thick near our front door!

options.text: Do not use the front door. Evacuate the house through the back door or kitchen window, staying far away from the wire.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Using alternative exits avoids the live wire blocking the front driveway, ensuring safe evacuation.

options.text: Jump directly over the sparking wire to escape through the front gate.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Attempting to jump over live wires risks touching them or stepping on electrified ground, which is fatal.

options.text: Wait inside the house until the fire burns itself out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Staying inside a house with a nearby burning wall leads to trapping and smoke inhalation.

options.text: Open all the front windows to clear the smoke.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Opening front windows feeds the fire oxygen and draws smoke directly into the house.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: We evacuated through the backyard gate. Me and my brother are in the back alley now. We can see the black smoke over the roof.

options.text: Stay in the back alley. Do not try to walk back to the front street near the wires. Keep safe.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Staying in the safe zone prevents accidental contact with live wires or falling embers.

options.text: Run to the front street to watch the fire truck arrive.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Moving back to the front street exposes the caller to the live wire and falling sparks.

options.text: Try to climb over the neighbor's metal fence to get a better look.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Metal fences can become electrified if live wires touch them, making climbing extremely risky.

options.text: Throw stones at the power line to break it completely.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Throwing stones does not help and can cause the line to move unpredictably, spreading the hazard.

transcript_en.speaker: Caller
transcript_en.text: We are waiting in the alley. The neighbors are also out here. Is help coming?

options.text: Yes. I am dispatching BFP to extinguish the fence fire, and PNP to secure the street block around the live wire.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Dispatching BFP to extinguish the fire and PNP to block traffic and secure the live wire hazard is correct.

options.text: I am sending MDRRMO medical only. Go back inside the house to wait.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Medical units cannot handle fires or live wires, and re-entering the house is highly dangerous.

options.text: I will send PNP only. Go touch the wire with a dry stick.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Touching power lines is extremely dangerous and potentially fatal.

options.text: Do not dispatch anyone. Power outages are normal.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Failing to dispatch assistance during active fire and electrical hazards is highly negligent.
